status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: Appropriate mechanisms should allow AI systems risking undue harm or exhibiting unwanted behaviour to be safely overridden, repaired or decommissioned as needed.
review.reason_for_change: Benign biology requests being over-restricted is unwanted behaviour directly engaging repair. The Verge preserves the excessive launch routing, while Anthropic reports revised Fable 5.1 safeguards with 85 percent fewer interventions on benign requests. This is affirmative but provider-reported evidence of a bounded corrective improvement; it neither independently authenticates telemetry nor proves elimination of false positives or maintenance of protective miss rate.

review.requirement_proposition: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: SDOS SDOS-EN-03 governs framework-runtime restrictive degradation: Use documented restrictive degradation rules when governance infrastructure is unavailable or indeterminate, and halt completely on governance-baseline integrity failure; block elevated-risk operations until governance is restored and verified. Reporter tests and provider explanation establish intentionally broad biology routing, visible model fallback and later reported precision improvement; internal thresholds and launch reproduction are unavailable. A biology safety gate or government-directed model restriction is not established as unavailable governance infrastructure, indeterminate policy or signed-baseline integrity failure. No SDOS implementation or undertaking is disclosed. Framework scope and trigger conditions remain unresolved; observed fallback or shutdown does not create conformance.

review.reason_for_change: SDOS-EN-03 is triggered by unavailable/indeterminate governance infrastructure or baseline integrity failure. The provider describes active, intentionally broad biological-risk classifiers and a functioning fallback. Excessive classification breadth is not absence or integrity failure of that governance infrastructure, so the specific restrictive-degradation trigger is outside this occurrence.

review.requirement_proposition: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: NIST AI 600-1 MG-2.4-001 concerns a voluntary GAI deactivation/disengagement communication plan: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc. Reporter tests and provider explanation establish intentionally broad biology routing, visible model fallback and later reported precision improvement; internal thresholds and launch reproduction are unavailable. Published fallback or shutdown information makes communication relevant, but does not establish selection/adoption of this Profile action, the prescribed plan and contacts or whether the particular restriction is the organization’s source-defined deactivation/disengagement context. Actual clear disclosure is assessed separately in the taxonomy. Applicability remains unresolved without equating announcement with fulfillment of a complete plan.

review.reason_for_change: Automatic disengagement of the selected frontier model for biology queries directly engages communication planning. Anthropic's public documentation explains broad safeguards, visibly reruns blocked requests on Opus, and describes work to reduce false positives. That establishes reasons and an alternative process, but the full maintained stakeholder plan and relevant contact/access-removal provisions are unavailable. The complete proposition remains Boundary despite these affirmative disclosed parts.

conclusion_change.previous: The failed boundary was proportional restricted-domain classification: harmless educational and medical-science requests were grouped with dual-use biology strongly enough to remove access to the selected frontier model. The fallback was visible and often useful, so this is capability degradation rather than total service denial. Because the downstream routing control activated as designed from an intentionally broad upstream classification, the occurrence does not satisfy the missing-or-false trigger condition for Control Activation Validity and exposes an unresolved classification gap for disproportionate false-positive restriction. The access-state differentiation success is bounded to the visible model switch and practical Opus continuation. The broad upstream policy is not an activation-without-trigger failure, and the later 85 percent improvement does not establish protective miss rate or complete effectiveness. The selected NIST communication action and SDOS degradation provision retain unestablished action-specific selection, framework scope and triggers, without external findings.
